stories.headline: Assam Cabinet Clears Defence Park, CBI Flood Probe, ₹2,440 Paddy Rate; Tightens Polygamy Rules
stories.title: Assam Cabinet Clears Defence Park, CBI Flood Probe, ₹2,440 Paddy Rate; Tightens Polygamy Rules
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'cabinet clears' in title weight 44
article_sentences: GUWAHATI: The Assam Cabinet has taken several crucial decisions pertaining to polygamy, defence park, ropeway, Zubeen Kshetra, CBI probe into the recent flashfood in Charaideo and Sivasagar, paddy procurement, etc.

Presided by Chief Minister Dr Himanta Biswa Sarma, the cabinet on Tuesday decided that departmental proceedings would be initiated against any government official found to have indulged in polygamy with proof, besides dismissing such officials and debarring them from any future government employment.
Civil Service Conduct Rules regarding the matter too received nod from the cabinet.

In order to enable Assam capture a slice of the growing defence production industry in the country, the cabinet also okayed handing over 6,000 bigha of land near Nellie in Morigaon district to the Industries & Commerce Department.
The land would be used for setting up a defence park where defence industries could be set up.
In another crucial move, the cabinet also gave nod to signing of a memorandum of understanding (MoU) by the Government of Assam with the Centre for ropeways.
A dedicated Ropeway Development Authority would be set up, where the Centre would hold 51% stake and the state government 49%.

Further, in addition to the ongoing ropeway project from Kamakhya railway station to Kamakhya temple atop Nilachal Hills, new ropeway projects would be taken up between Gangananagar and Bhubon Pahar in Barak Valley, Agnigarh Pahar and Bharavi Mandir in Sonitpur district, and at Jatinga in Dima Hasao district.
The cabinet also decided to hand over the probe into the flashfloods in Charaideo and Sivasagar districts earlier this year to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), and find the root cause.
Dispur will submit a request to the CBI within the next 10 days to take up the case.
Clearing land-related confusion regarding Zubeen Kshetra, the cabinet has given nod to regularising two bighas of land adjacent to the site after acquisition.
The private party owning the land has been given an alternative site.

stories.headline: Election Observer supervises final phase of randomization
stories.title: Election Observer supervises final phase of randomization
stories.summary: The final phase focused on the automated allotment of Polling Personnel Officer 2 (PO2) staff to individual polling booths and the impartial assignment of micro-observers across all notified polling stations.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The final phase focused on the automated allotment of Polling Personnel Officer 2 (PO2) staff to individual polling booths and the impartial assignment of micro-observers across all notified polling stations.

Puttaparthi: District election authorities in Sri Sathya Sai district successfully completed the third phase of the computer-based randomization process on Tuesday at the mini-conference hall in the Puttaparthi Collectorate to finalize polling staff assignments for the upcoming ZPTC and MPTC elections.
The entire process was conducted using specialized computer software to guarantee absolute transparency, eliminating any scope for manual intervention or political bias.
Election Observer P Arun Babu personally supervised the proceedings to ensure strict compliance with the Model Code of Conduct and State Election Commission guidelines.
Joint Collector Maurya Bharadwaj coordinated the software operations and oversaw the assignment of personnel across designated booths.
District Revenue Officer (DRO) P Kondaiah reviewed administrative logistics, staff availability, and polling station preparations.
Technical management was handled by NIC staff member M Ravi Krishna and e-District Manager S Harish Kumar, ensuring that the computerized allocation proceeded seamlessly without technical glitches.
Following the completion of the randomization, officials confirmed that deployment orders will be issued to the selected personnel immediately.

The district administration reiterated its commitment to conducting free, fair, and peaceful voting across all rural territorial constituencies on Thursday, November 5, with comprehensive administrative and security arrangements fully in place.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Asserts Right to Protest Must Not Lead to Indefinite Occupation of Public Spaces
stories.title: Supreme Court Asserts Right to Protest Must Not Lead to Indefinite Occupation of Public Spaces
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: New Delhi, Nov 3: The Supreme Court on Tuesday orally observed that the right to protest cannot be exercised by occupying a designated protest site indefinitely, stressing that such places must be allotted for specified periods to ensure that other groups also get an opportunity to exercise their constitutional rights.

A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana made the observations while hearing a batch of petitions arising from the October protests in Delhi against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar.
"You cannot occupy a site for all time to come.
There are other protesters.
Where will the farmers go?
Where will the workers go?
Where will the trade unions go?
Where will the homeless go?
Everybody has a right to protest," the apex court remarked.

It further observed that protest sites must be made available to different groups for designated periods, adding that no organisation could claim an exclusive right over a public space merely because it had occupied it first.
"There may be one site or two, but everybody has a right to protest.
You cannot exclude other people merely because you have occupied the site," the CJI-led Bench said.
